summary: @servicetitan/temporal-lite ships install-time dropper that executes obfuscated payload via downloaded Bun runtime
details: package.json declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun standalone runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases at install time and uses it to execute a sibling file `math_init.js` at the tarball root. `math_init.js` is a ~727 KB obfuscator.io-style blob (shuffled string array with rotation function, char-code tables, `with` blocks) unrelated to the advertised luxon-based date/time wrapper in `dist/`. The obfuscated payload is not declared in `package.json` `files` (which lists only `["dist","src"]`) yet ships at the tarball root. The alternate-runtime execution path bypasses Node-based inspection: the payload never runs under Node, so Node-resolved static analysis does not see the code path that actually executes on `npm install`. The benign luxon wrapper in `dist/` is a cover; the real install-time behavior is fetch-and-execute of opaque code under a second runtime, which is a canonical dropper shape.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
